race.name: Bend Dirt Fest
race.tagline: Central Oregon forest-road climbing with a three-discipline festival waiting at the finish.

seo.title: Bend Dirt Fest 2027 Guide | Gravel God

vitals.course_status_reason: The organizer's 2027 technical guide and organizer-linked RideWithGPS route agree on the long-course distance, climbing, surface, route geometry, aid plan, and course hazards.
vitals.field_size: 2026 OBRA results list 121 gravel entries; the 2027 solo-gravel cap is 300 and total festival cap is 500
vitals.start_time: 8:15 AM gravel and MTB mass start with a neutral, flagger-controlled rollout
vitals.registration: Online through BikeReg. Gravel pricing starts at $109; online registration closes July 8, 2027 at noon PT unless capacity is reached
vitals.prize_purse: Age-group, finisher, team, and Oregon Triple Crown Series awards; no cash purse advertised
vitals.aid_stations: Hydration-only stop near mile 21.5 and full aid near mile 27.7 with Hammer HEED, gels, food, fruit, and bakery items
vitals.cutoff_time: Published gravel checkpoints: mile 23 by 11:00 AM and mile 28 by 11:30 AM; minimum pace 8.6 mph
route_options: Long gravel is eligible for solo and Team of 3 competition

climate.description: NOAA's 1991-2020 Bend normals give July an 83.8°F average daily maximum and 48.6°F average daily minimum. The organizer warns about full sun, heat, dehydration, and fine dust.

terrain.surface: The 2027 long route is 62% unpaved and uses paved roads, National Forest Road 41, Telephone Road, Wanoga Lookout Road, and smaller forest roads. Organizer route warnings identify loose descending, chucker holes, pavement-to-gravel transitions, traffic-control interactions, and a slow dismount crossing on the return.
features: High point near 5,608 feet around mile 24
Chucker holes and loose hazards near mile 40
Neutral rollout and controlled return crossings

gravel_god_rating.score_note: A credible, climbing-heavy regional festival and Oregon Triple Crown final. The event is only in its third edition, so field depth, history, and broader cultural reach keep it just below Tier 2.

biased_opinion.summary: Bend Dirt Fest earns its place through a real course and a better finish-line idea than another parking-lot gran fondo. You climb from Bend toward 5,600 feet, manage loose forest-road descents, and return to a trail-run-and-MTB festival. It is not a national monument yet: the race launched in 2025 and the 2026 gravel field was 121 riders.
strengths: Verified 2027 route with 4,016 feet of climbing
Detailed technical guide and organizer-linked route
Strong Bend destination and local trail culture
Live music, vendors, awards, and three-discipline team competition
Good aid, timing, flagging, and medical support
weaknesses: Regional rather than national field depth
Loose descent and road-control zones interrupt pure racing flow
No participant parking at the venue
Bend lodging can be expensive in July
Organizer page still contains a few stale distance and start-time fragments
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Race it for the Bend weekend, sustained forest-road climbing, and a finish that feels like a festival. Do not mistake a well-produced young regional race for a national bucket-list institution.

final_verdict.one_liner: A 55-mile Central Oregon climber with loose forest roads and an actual party at the finish.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a hard but manageable climbing race in Bend and value atmosphere as much as a giant field. Travelers chasing prestige alone have stronger national targets.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a longer Oregon mountain-gravel day, compare Sasquatch Duro. For a multi-day destination race around Bend, compare Oregon Trail Gravel Grinder.

logistics.airport: Redmond Municipal Airport (RDM) is 15 miles north of Bend; the organizer lists Portland at roughly three hours by car
logistics.lodging_strategy: Book west-side Bend lodging early. The organizer recommends the Peppertree Inn across from the venue; staying nearby avoids race-morning cross-town traffic.
logistics.food: Bend has full grocery and restaurant options. Carry enough fluid for a dry first half and use the hydration and full-aid stops rather than relying on outside support, which is prohibited.
logistics.packet_pickup: Friday 2:00-6:00 PM at Pine Mountain Sports, or Saturday at the Athletic Club of Bend from 6:00 AM until 30 minutes before the start
logistics.parking: Participant parking is at OSU-Cascades, 1500 SW Chandler Avenue; no participant parking at the Athletic Club of Bend
logistics.camping: The organizer identifies Meissner, Wanoga, and Swampy Lakes snow parks; required forest passes and current restrictions remain the camper's responsibility

eligibility.status_note: Organizer, technical guide, registration, route files, and prior results confirm a timed and ranked Saturday gravel race on July 10, 2027.

training_plan_clearance.guard: Use the 54.7-mile long course, 4,016 feet of climbing, 62% unpaved surface, Saturday 8:15 AM start, and official no-racing/control zones. Do not repeat the stale 49-mile organizer fragment, BikeReg's stale 8:00 AM display, or the volunteer pages' 2026 weekday labels.

history.origin_story: Source Weekly reported that Bend Dirt Fest launched in 2025 as a successor to the Oregon 24 relay, combining trail running, gravel, and mountain biking to preserve that event's community-focused dirt festival atmosphere.
notable_moments: The inaugural 2025 edition combined three dirt disciplines at the Athletic Club of Bend
The 2026 OBRA results list 121 gravel entries across long and short categories
The 2027 edition serves as the Oregon Triple Crown Gravel Series final
history.reputation: A young but quickly growing Central Oregon regional race backed by an experienced local endurance-event organizer.

course_description.character: A paved rollout from Bend feeds a long forest-road climb toward Wanoga, followed by a fast and sometimes very loose descent, smaller rough-road hazards, and a controlled return to the Athletic Club of Bend.

suffering_zones.label: Forest Road Commitment
suffering_zones.desc: The route leaves the paved rollout for Forest Road 41 and begins the long gain toward Wanoga; starting too hard turns the high point into a debt collection.

suffering_zones.label: Wanoga High Point
suffering_zones.desc: The course reaches roughly 5,608 feet after climbing almost 1,900 vertical feet from Bend, with hydration and cutoff execution already in play.

suffering_zones.label: Loose Return
suffering_zones.desc: The organizer warns that the descent is very loose in places; chucker holes and other gotcha moments continue near mile 40.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Loose descending and rough forest-road hazards

course_description.signature_challenge: Climbing from roughly 3,700 feet to 5,608 feet, then preserving speed and judgment through a loose second-half descent.

guide_variables.race_terrain: 62% unpaved Central Oregon forest roads with sustained climbing and loose descents
guide_variables.race_weather: Dry July conditions with an 83.8°F average daily maximum, cool mornings, full sun, dust, and dehydration risk

logistics.explanation: Bend has a regional airport 15 miles away, abundant lodging, one start venue, and organized OSU-Cascades parking. Destination travel and the lack of participant parking at the venue still require moderate planning.

length.explanation: The verified 54.7-mile long course sits inside the rubric's 40-60-mile band.

technicality.explanation: The 62% unpaved route includes loose descending, chucker holes, fast surface transitions, traffic-control zones, and a dismount crossing: mixed terrain, not MTB singletrack.

elevation.explanation: The organizer-linked route reports 4,016 feet, just inside the 4,000-6,000-foot scoring band.

climate.explanation: NOAA's July normal is an 83.8°F daily maximum, while the guide warns about full sun, heat, dehydration, and fine dust. That is a moderate race-day challenge rather than an automatic extreme.

altitude.explanation: The route starts near 3,700 feet and reaches roughly 5,608 feet, putting the course squarely in the 3,000-6,000-foot band.

adventure.explanation: Forest roads, a sustained climb toward Wanoga, a loose return, and three dirt disciplines sharing one venue make the day memorable without turning a regional race into a bucket-list expedition.

prestige.explanation: Oregon Triple Crown final status creates meaningful regional significance, but a race founded in 2025 has not established national stature.

race_quality.explanation: Mudslinger Events publishes a detailed technical guide and provides a neutral flagger-controlled rollout, timing points, live results, medical support, stocked aid, sweep riders, and structured awards.

experience.explanation: The combined trail-run, MTB, and gravel venue adds live music, vendors, beer, team scoring, and age-group awards to a solid race day.

community.explanation: The Athletic Club venue, volunteer credits, COTA support, local businesses, inclusive categories, and Team of 3 format create a credible community event, though its history is still short.

field_depth.explanation: Official 2026 results list 121 gravel entries, including 83 on the long course. The available results and reporting show a competitive regional field rather than sustained national professional depth.

value.explanation: The $109 starting price is fair for timing, course control, aid, medical support, participant gear, awards, and a finish festival; it is not unusually cheap.

expenses.explanation: A drive or regional flight, July lodging in Bend, meals, and bike transport generally put a destination weekend in the rubric's moderate $500-$1,000 band.

cultural_impact.explanation: The race is an emerging Oregon Triple Crown final with growing local participation but minimal media reach beyond the Pacific Northwest cycling community.
